content.thinking:
The rtlwifi path maps queue → endpoint **number** (not descriptor index), then uses `usb_sndbulkpipe(udev, ep)`. This is a "hard-coded endpoint address" pattern — the driver doesn't read `endpoint[]` with an assumed index. Instead it uses hard-coded endpoint numbers like 2, 3, 5 (endpoint addresses). If the device lacks those endpoints, `usb_bulk_msg` to an invalid pipe would fail but not OOB-read kernel memory. That's a different (weaker) issue — the pipe references an endpoint address that may not exist; URB submission would fail. Not a NULL-deref/OOB read of the endpoint array. So rtlwifi is safe with respect to the seed mechanism.

Now, back to the fixed-index candidates found:
1. `drivers/net/usb/cdc-phonet.c:366-375` — endpoint[0], endpoint[1] read after validating `bNumEndpoints == 2` for the chosen data_desc. SAFE (validated).
2. `drivers/net/usb/cdc_ether.c:297` — endpoint[0] after `bNumEndpoints == 1` check. SAFE.
3. `drivers/net/usb/qmi_wwan.c:674` — `dev->status = &info->control->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0];` — need to check whether bNumEndpoints of control interface is validated. This is the classic usbnet status-endpoint pattern. Let me look at qmi_wwan.c more closely. In upstream, qmi_wwan_bind does check... Let me read the full bind function of qmi_wwan.c.

Also check cdc_ncm.c (683 uses a loop with bNumEndpoints bound, safe), and sierra_net.c line 681 uses numendpoints. Let me check sierra_net.c around 681.

Also check hso.c:3148 — loop `for (i = 0; i < iface->desc.bNumEndpoints; i++)` safe. ipheth.c:462 — loop with bNumEndpoints, safe.
